reliability.summary: Below-average reliability for the Dart. The 2.4L Tigershark is known for burning oil, and a manual is tiring in stop-and-go delivery driving. Its pluses are that it's local, has fresh brakes, clutch and tires, and has one owner.
issues: 2.4L Tigershark oil consumption (Chrysler issued a service bulletin and extended the warranty on some cars); check how often it needs topping up
Electrical and module faults (instrument cluster, TIPM) are common on Darts
Manual in town: lots of clutch work for delivery stop-and-go, though the clutch was just replaced
Open recalls are common on 2013–2016 Darts (check by VIN)
checks: Get the VIN: check recalls and run a history report
Check the oil level and look for blue smoke on startup
Confirm the clean title is in the seller's name, and the price ($5,000 vs $6,000 OBO)
Ask for receipts for the clutch, brakes and tires
Pre-purchase inspection; it's local, so easy to do

reliability.summary: The 3rd-gen Prius is one of the most durable cars made, but this one is a SALVAGE-title car repaired after a right-front collision, at 190k miles. Its real condition depends on the repair quality and the hybrid battery's health - both need the inspection.
issues: Front-end crash repair quality (frame rail, suspension, alignment)
Hybrid battery wear at ~190k
Inverter coolant pump / cooling leaks after a front hit
EGR system clogging and head-gasket wear at high miles (2010-2015 1.8L)
Salvage title: limited insurance, lower resale
checks: Insurance quote with the VIN first
Toyota of Ridgecrest $185 inspection incl. hybrid battery test
Frame rail/apron and alignment
No warning lights; airbag light goes out after startup
Salvage inspection/registration done; title in seller's name
Oil and coolant levels

reliability.summary: Good. Late 3rd-gen Fit (2015 launch-year bugs mostly fixed). Simple non-turbo 1.5L, cheap parts. Lowest NHTSA complaint count of your shortlist. Main risk is the CVT at 112k.
issues: CVT hesitation/whine/judder - most-reported serious issue
Some oil consumption reports
Starter and ignition coil failures (cheap fixes)
A/C recharge / blower motor issues
Recalls: fuel pump (stall), rearview camera (x2), passenger seat weight sensor/airbag (2026)
checks: Ask for CVT fluid change records (should have 1-2 by 112k)
Test drive: smooth pull from a stop, no whine or slip feeling
Check oil level on dipstick
A/C cold after 15 min
Run VIN: are the 4 recalls done? (free at Honda dealer)

reliability.summary: 8th-gen Accord with the 2.4L 4-cylinder and lower miles than most cars at this price. Solid in-town car; the 2008–2010 2.4L can burn oil.
issues: 2008–2010 2.4L oil consumption (piston rings); check the oil level and ask how often it's topped up
Rear brakes wear fast on this generation
A/C compressor failures are common
VTC actuator rattle on cold start
checks: Get the VIN and check recalls (airbag inflator recalls were common on Hondas)
Check the oil level and look for blue smoke
Run the A/C for 15 minutes
Listen for a rattle on a cold start
Pre-purchase inspection

reliability.summary: Loaded gen-3 Prius from a private seller with smog done. Same 177k-mile gen-3 risks.
issues: EGR valve/cooler clogging can lead to head-gasket failure around 150–200k (ask if the EGR has been cleaned)
Inverter coolant pump (covered by a recall; check it was done)
Hybrid battery age: budget about $1,500–2,500 for a refurbished pack if it weakens
Brake booster/actuator failure on some cars
checks: Run the VIN (it's in the listing) for history
Run the VIN for open recalls
Hybrid battery health scan (Dr. Prius app + OBD reader, or Toyota of Ridgecrest)
Check coolant level and for white smoke / overheating (head gasket)
Pre-purchase inspection before paying

reliability.summary: Gen-3 Prius with low miles for the price and a clean history. The Prius is the best DoorDash car on gas cost.

reliability.summary: The 2012-17 Veloster's 1.6L is average; the optional dual-clutch automatic can be jerky and costly to fix. Ask which transmission it has.
issues: Dual-clutch (EcoShift) transmission problems if equipped
Carbon buildup on the direct-injected 1.6L
Hatch/door rattles
Clutch wear on manuals
checks: Title status and name
Which transmission (6-speed auto, dual-clutch, or manual)
No check-engine light; scan for codes
A/C cold

reliability.summary: Average for this year: the 2006-2009 1.8L Civic can crack its engine block (coolant loss/overheating), usually fixed long ago if it happened. Low miles for the age and one owner help.
issues: Cracked engine block (1.8L R18, 2006-09) - check coolant carefully
Peeling clear coat in sun
Rear tire wear (suspension geometry)
Takata airbag recalls
checks: Coolant level and any crust near the block/thermostat; ask if the block was ever replaced
Run VIN: Takata airbag recalls done?
A/C cold
Smooth shifts (5-speed automatic)
Ask for the smog certificate

reliability.summary: The 2014-18 Forte with the 1.8L is average: simple and cheap to fix, not part of the big Kia/Hyundai 2.0/2.4 engine recalls, but check for oil use at high miles.
issues: Oil consumption at high mileage
Steering coupler clunk (fix is cheap)
A/C condenser
Accident on record - inspect repairs
checks: No check-engine light; scan for codes
Oil level
Steering clunk over bumps
Body/paint around the repaired area

reliability.summary: The 9th-gen (2012-15) Civic Hybrid's 1.5L engine and CVT are generally solid and it switched to a lithium-ion battery. Mileage puts the battery and CVT near the point where they need checking.
issues: Hybrid (IMA) battery wear at high mileage
CVT judder or slipping
A/C compressor
12-volt battery drain
checks: Hybrid battery health test; ask about IMA/battery history
No IMA or check-engine lights; scan for stored codes
CVT smooth from a stop, no shudder
A/C cold
Run VIN for open recalls

reliability.summary: Good. Simple 1.6L with a 6-speed automatic (no CVT), cheap to insure and fix - and about $3,900 less than the Ridgecrest Accent, with no accidents reported.
issues: 1.6L GDI carbon buildup / oil consumption at high miles
Steering coupler clunk
3 owners - ask for service history
checks: Check oil level
Steering: any clunk turning lock to lock
Get dealer fees in writing
Run VIN for recalls

reliability.summary: Same as the 2008: an excellent design, but at 20 years old the hybrid battery and brake actuator are the big-ticket risks. Priced low enough to leave room for a battery if needed.
issues: Hybrid battery capacity loss with age
Brake actuator / ABS pump failure
Combination meter failure
Oil consumption / EGR at high miles
checks: Hybrid battery health test before buying
No triangle/ABS/check-engine lights
Confirm the smog certificate date
Confirm availability by phone before the 2-hour drive

reliability.summary: Gen-2 Prius drivetrain is very durable, but at 172k the original hybrid battery is near the end of its typical life, and the price reflects that.
issues: Hybrid battery degradation (~150-200k)
Inverter coolant pump failure
Burning oil / head gasket on high-mileage 1NZ-FXE
Combination meter (dash display) going dark
Brake actuator failure
checks: Hybrid battery test (Dr. Prius life test)
Watch dash for triangle warning / 'check hybrid system'
Inverter coolant pump running (listen at hood with car READY)
Oil level
Registration back-fee amount and smog certificate

reliability.summary: The 2013 Civic (1.8L R18, 5-speed auto) is one of the more reliable used compacts; 2013 fixed most of the 2012 redesign complaints. At 140k it needs its maintenance history checked.
issues: A/C compressor / condenser failures
Engine mount wear (vibration at idle)
Valve adjustment due ~100-110k if never done
Takata airbag recall - confirm completed
checks: Title in seller's name and matches VIN
Run VIN for recalls (Takata)
A/C cold at idle in heat
Vibration at idle in Drive (mounts)
Ask for valve adjustment / transmission fluid service records

reliability.summary: Good. The 9th-gen Corolla (2003-2008) with the 1.8L and 4-speed automatic is famously hard to kill, and this one has relatively low miles and a clean history.
issues: Some 2005-2008 1.8L engines burn oil at high miles
Water pump and A/C wear
Basic, older safety equipment (side airbags optional)
checks: Check the oil level and ask how often it's topped up
A/C cold after 15 min
Get dealer fees in writing (CarGurus says fees not disclosed)
Run VIN for Takata airbag recall completion

reliability.summary: Good. The 2009-2013 Fit with the 1.5L and a conventional 5-speed automatic (not a CVT) is one of the most dependable small cars of its era - same family as your 2018 Fit pick, for about half the price.
issues: Ignition coil and A/C compressor failures at high miles
Engine mounts wear
Rear drum brakes / suspension wear at 165k
checks: Ask what the reported accident was
A/C cold after 15 min
Service records (timing chain engine, but oil changes matter)
Run VIN for recalls (driver's window switch, airbag)

reliability.summary: Average given its age: the Camry Hybrid's drivetrain is durable, but at 18 years the hybrid battery is the big risk (refurbished pack roughly $1,500-3,000), and the 2007-2009 Camrys share the sticky-dashboard problem.
issues: Hybrid battery capacity loss with age
Inverter coolant pump failure (hybrid system warning)
Sticky/melting dashboard in heat
Brake actuator wear
checks: Hybrid battery health test at an independent hybrid shop
No hybrid-system, check-engine or ABS warnings
A/C cold (electric compressor)
Run VIN for recalls (floor mat/accelerator, window switch)

reliability.summary: Good. The 1st-gen Mazda3 (2010-2013) with the 2.0L and 5-speed automatic is a dependable, simple compact - and this one has low miles and no accidents. Not as frugal as the newer Skyactiv Mazda3, but cheap to run.
issues: Engine mounts wear (vibration at idle)
Clear-coat / sun-faded paint and cracked dash in desert heat
A/C and power steering pump issues reported at higher miles
Ignition coil failures
checks: Ask for photos and the VIN-confirmed body style
Vibration at idle in Drive (motor mounts)
A/C cold after 15 min
Run VIN for recalls

reliability.summary: The 2nd-gen Prius is one of the most reliable cars ever built, but this one is 18 years old: the main risk is the hybrid battery (a refurbished pack is roughly $1,500-3,000) and other age-related hybrid parts.
issues: Hybrid battery capacity loss with age
Brake actuator / ABS pump failure (expensive)
Combination meter (dash display) failure
Some 1.5L engines burn oil; EGR clogging at high miles
checks: Hybrid battery health test at an independent hybrid shop (worth paying for)
No warning lights (triangle / ABS / check engine)
Dash display works
Ask the dealer what the 3-day return terms are (CARS Act)

reliability.summary: Good. Simple 1.6L with a conventional 6-speed automatic (no CVT). Cheap parts, cheap insurance. Main unknowns on this car: the reported accident and rental-fleet use.
issues: 1.6L GDI: some carbon buildup / oil consumption at high miles
Ex-rental: hard use, often only basic maintenance
Steering coupler noise (clunk) on this generation
A/C: check it stays cold
checks: Get the AutoCheck report: how bad was the accident? airbags?
Inspection: frame, panel gaps, paint overspray, alignment
Check oil level/consumption
Run VIN for open recalls (Hyundai dealer)

reliability.summary: Good. 3rd-gen Mazda3 (2014-2018) with the 2.0L Skyactiv and a conventional 6-speed automatic (no CVT) is one of the more reliable compacts of its era, and the lowest-mileage car on your list. 30 city / 40 hwy MPG.
issues: Mazda Connect touchscreen 'ghost touch' / freezing (2014-2016 Grand Touring)
A/C condenser or compressor failures reported
Some carbon buildup on direct-injection engines at higher miles
Aftermarket/aesthetic mods: check nothing affects smog or insurance
Recalls (4): fuel tank, parking-brake caliper (water can enter), rearview camera - confirm done by VIN
checks: Confirm the smog certificate date (valid 90 days)
Test the infotainment screen and backup camera
A/C cold after 15 min
Look at the 'few small dents' and any mod wiring
Run VIN for open recalls
